clue.text: Argument draining for conciliation service

indicators.note: draining the word for empties it of its inside, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: ACAS is the UK's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which mediates in workplace disputes

explanation.surface: A row breaks out as both sides give up on the mediation service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draining' takes the middle letter out of 'for', leaving its outer pair. 'Conciliation service' is a real British body, not a description of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or brawl, so it is a synonym for an argument.

clue.text: Don't eat hat for a quickie

parts.note: to go without food is to fast
a bowler is a round, hard felt hat

explanation.surface: Advice to skip your meal and grab a hat for a hurried exit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a FAST BOWLER delivers the ball at high speed; 'quickie' is cricket slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang calls a pace bowler a quickie, because the deliveries come down at speed.

clue.text: Old article, wood, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the pieces are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: an is the indefinite article; teak is a hard tropical wood

explanation.surface: A dealer's patter describing an old piece of wooden furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: AN plus TEAK, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antique is old, especially a valued object from an earlier era.

clue.text: Hypothetical man of letters

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adjective meaning theoretical and as a noun for a scholarly person.

clue.text: Mayo destination cancelled, as imitation

parts.note: Knock in County Mayo, Ireland, is a pilgrimage shrine with its own airport
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: A trip to the west of Ireland is called off, making it a sham journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Knock is a small town in County Mayo, Ireland, famous for its Marian shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock-off is a cheap copy of a branded product, so an imitation.

clue.text: A lot then? Hardly!

parts.note: a sarcastic query about quantity met by an emphatic denial that even a small amount is true

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of saying not at all, the opposite of a lot.

clue.text: Stuff about English royal's heart that's rich

indicators.note: about means the word for stuff goes around the next piece

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Feeding a member of the royal family a lavish dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAM goes round E to make CREAM, then Y, the middle letter of 'royal', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Creamy food is full of fat and dairy, which is what rich means of food.

clue.text: I'm heading for exit after old bag becomes ex

indicators.note: after puts the I'm and exit pieces behind the old bag pieces

parts.note: a net is a mesh bag
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone leaving the room after an insult to their former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: O and NET come first, then IM and E, the first letter of 'exit'. 'Old bag' looks like an insult but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, which is what ex means as a prefix or adjective.

clue.text: About time sort of fire lit phosphorus, needing cigarette

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the time piece
sort of signals that the letters of fire lit are to be sorted into a new order

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A smoker strikes a match to light up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns FIRELIT into FILTERI, which goes round T, and P follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A filter tip is a cigarette with a filter at the mouth end, a name used for the cigarette itself.

clue.text: Point at vehicle going the wrong way, driver needing this?

parts.note: S is the compass point south
taken as written

indicators.note: a vehicle going the wrong way suggests reading its word backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone points at a car heading against the traffic, whose driver must be lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost driver going the wrong way needs a satellite navigation device to find the route.

clue.text: Light present in tin, perhaps, having removed lid

indicators.note: in places the word for present inside the trimmed metal
the lid of a word is its first letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: tin is an example of a metal
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A light shines from inside a tin can after the lid comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having removed lid' drops the first letter of the metal, leaving ETAL, which 'in' then opens to take the word for present.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicately light and airy, as if not of this world.

clue.text: Upset tummies quake by the end of a close match

definitions.text: the end of a close match

indicators.note: upset signals that the letters of the following words are to be overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous fan's stomach churns as the game goes to the wire.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase was coined by football manager Alex Ferguson for the nerve-racking final minutes of a tight contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the tense closing stage of a tight contest, when nerves are frayed.

clue.text: Naked stills exploited to sell a sordid story

indicators.note: exploited suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Nude photographs are being used by someone hawking scandal to the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and tell is to sell the story of an affair to the press.

clue.text: Over-refinement in words generating icy riposte

indicators.note: generating suggests the letters are produced afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A fussy, overwrought choice of words provokes a cold retort.
explanation.definitionFit: Preciosity is excessive refinement or affectation in language.

clue.text: Promote what sounds like right scandal?

indicators.note: what sounds like signals that the pieces are heard spoken

parts.note: right means proper, and gate is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: Asking whether promoting something counts as a genuine scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: PROPER plus GATE, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate an idea is to spread and promote it.

clue.text: See 24
Stagger in with sot, reeling into tree

indicators.note: into places the rearranged letters within the tree

parts.note: the ash is a tree

indicators.note: a reeling drunk staggers, signalling the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A drunkard stumbles in and crashes into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeling' rearranges 'in' and 'sot' to STONI; 'Stagger' looks like the drunk's stumbling but is the definition, meaning amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze them, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Nothing works — oh dear!

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
ops is short for operations, which are works

explanation.surface: A dismayed cry as nothing works.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild dismay at a mistake or mishap.

clue.text: Publicity about why rich embroidery is at too high a cost

indicators.note: about means the publicity letters go round the next piece

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

indicators.note: embroidery means the letters of rich are embellished into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A publicist asks why a lavish piece of embroidery cost so much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidery' reworks 'rich' into RHIC; a Pyrrhic victory is named after King Pyrrhus, whose wins against Rome ruined his army.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pyrrhic victory is won at such cost that it is hardly worth it.

clue.text: Snoo?

parts.note: these four letters are the first part of a word for a nap, so they are only part of a sleeping word

explanation.definitionFit: Half asleep means drowsy, and the clue shows only part of a word meaning a nap.

clue.text: Changed 'em over

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
over means finished, ended

explanation.surface: Someone says they swapped them around.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or alter a text, so emended means changed.

clue.text: See 1
Cooler product for the 'ead?

indicators.note: 'ead is head with its H dropped, as a Cockney would say it, so the H is dropped here too

parts.note: a product for the head is a hair conditioner

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cooling gadget is really a treatment for the hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A product for the head is a hair conditioner; the dropped H in 'ead tells you to drop the H of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: An air conditioner cools a room, so it is a cooler.

clue.text: Wave's power

definitions.meaning: to wave is to swing to and fro

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to rock back and forth and also means influence over others.

clue.text: Hero getting cold among ebbing waves

indicators.note: among places the cold piece inside the waves piece
the sea ebbing goes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the waves are the sea
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A hero catches a chill wading in the receding tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' turns the waves backwards to give AES; the tide going out suits the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great Greek hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Computer operator having to take in place other than the aisle?

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's computer operating system
to take in food is to eat

explanation.surface: A computer user is about to eat on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: On a plane or train the alternative to an aisle seat is a seat by the window.

clue.text: Ring agencies at the centre right, not half clever!

indicators.note: at the centre means the central letters of agencies
not half means only half the word clever is used

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a central agency's cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: ENCI is the centre of 'agencies', then R, then CLE, half of 'clever'. 'Not half' is British slang for very much.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle is to surround, to form a ring around.

clue.text: Reserved seats unusual, as cheap

indicators.note: seats means the reserved piece holds the unusual piece within it

parts.note: a reserved person is shy
odd means unusual

explanation.surface: Booked theatre seats turn out to be oddly poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means poorly made, cheap and inferior.
